drivers.headline: Gold -0.69% over the last 5 sessions (Oct 9 → Oct 16: 4,193.37 → 4,164.52). Pushed lower mainly by: funds net -3.9K contracts (COT Oct 13); CPI y/y (Sep) 3.7% vs 3.6% fcst (Oct 14, hawkish); Core CPI m/m (Sep) 0.3% vs 0.2% fcst (Oct 14, hawkish); PPI m/m (Sep) 1.3% vs 0.5% fcst (Oct 15, hawkish). Working against it: DXY -0.37%; 10Y real yield -17bp; US 10Y -15bp.

lines.label: US dollar
lines.text: Dollar index (DXY) -0.37% (Oct 9 → Oct 16). A weaker dollar makes gold cheaper for non-US buyers → supportive.

lines.label: Real yields
lines.src: U.S. Treasury real yield curve (10Y TIPS)
lines.text: 10Y real yield -17bp to 2.74% (Oct 9 → Oct 16). Falling real yields lower the cost of holding gold (it pays no interest) → supportive.

lines.label: US 10Y yield
lines.text: US 10Y yield -15bp to 5.10% (Oct 9 → Oct 16). Bond yields falling = markets pricing less Fed tightening.

lines.label: Oil
lines.text: WTI crude +10.4% (Oct 9 → Oct 16). Higher oil lifts inflation fears: that can support gold as a hedge but also pushes the Fed to stay tight (mixed).

lines.label: Risk mood
lines.src: S&P 500 and VIX daily close, CNBC
lines.text: S&P 500 -1.9%, VIX +5.1 pts (Oct 9 → Oct 16). Risk-off: safe-haven demand helps gold.

lines.text: Managed money (funds) net -3.9K contracts to 107.1K; swap dealers (banks) net +0.9K to -224.1K; open interest +0.2K (report Oct 13). Funds were cutting longs / adding shorts → selling pressure.
